records.name: Pyridoxine for SGPL1 R222Q SPLIS
records.indication: SGPL1 R222Q sphingosine phosphate lyase insufficiency syndrome (SPLIS)
records.evidence_stage: individual uncontrolled human observation plus patient cells, enzyme, and genotype-specific mouse evidence
records.disposition: genotype-specific scientific watch; bounded desk diligence only
positive_evidence: Individual R222Q neurological and biochemical response reported after pyridoxine.
Patient-cell and recombinant-enzyme evidence supports cofactor responsiveness.
R222Q mouse model links pyridoxine availability to disease expression.
critical_boundaries: Individual uncontrolled human observation is not controlled efficacy.
JCI and earlier preprint are the same study lineage; earlier responder context is not independent replication of the new paper.
Diet-conditioned mouse prevention is not reversal of established renal disease.
Do not generalize R222Q findings to all SGPL1 genotypes.
Current manuscript describes a second R222Q patient relative to earlier work; no pooled treated/responder denominator inferred.
records.value_capture_assessment: Generic substance; no concrete exclusive asset or differentiated commercial capture route established.
records.comparator: Cash for development capital; existing mutation-specific repurposing candidates for desk priority.
records.next_decision_changing_question: Can a reproducible genotype-defined clinical proposition support a concrete attainable capture route?
records.next_information_step: Bounded public-record review of genotype-specific clinical observations, natural history, ownership, and claims.
records.financing_and_time: A desk conclusion can be reached without a development commitment; clinical milestone budget and timing are unknown.
disconfirming_evidence: Population or endpoints prevent an achievable milestone.

records.name: ATP1A3 prime editing for alternating hemiplegia of childhood
records.evidence_stage: two mouse disease models; neonatal treatment
positive_evidence: Molecular correction in two disease-variant models.
Functional phenotypic benefit following neonatal treatment.
critical_boundaries: Both mouse models treated at birth.
Later adult phenotype rescue does not show efficacy from treatment initiated in older symptomatic patients.
No human efficacy or clinical-ready asset package verified.
PubMed and PMC describe one Cell paper.
Five corrected cell variants do not establish in-vivo efficacy for five variants.
records.value_capture_assessment: Potentially proprietary approach, but platform, disease-specific, delivery, and package rights may require assembly; obtainability unknown.
records.comparator: Cash for development capital; existing neurological gene-delivery candidates with nearer information gates.
records.next_decision_changing_question: Is there an attainable integrated rights package and a clinically plausible treatment window?
records.next_information_step: Bounded public evidence and ownership review of variant scope, timing, delivery, and licensable package.
records.financing_and_time: Translational and manufacturing program likely substantial; no credible budget or calendar established for a human decision-changing milestone.
advance_conditions: Clinically feasible treatment window and delivery.
Financeable milestone tied to meaningful patient benefit.
disconfirming_evidence: Delivery cannot reproduce relevant CNS coverage in patients.
Rights cannot be assembled on viable terms.

records.name: VS-X4 STING inhibition for NGLY1 deficiency
records.evidence_stage: pharmacological and genetic evidence in inducible postnatal Ngly1 knockout mice
records.disposition: exact-asset preclinical watch; bounded access/rights desk diligence
positive_evidence: VS-X4 mitigated neurological disease and preserved Purkinje cells in the model.
Genetic Sting1 deletion supports pathway causality.
Exact named oral candidate rather than only a target hypothesis.
critical_boundaries: NGLY1 lifespan extension is demonstrated for genetic Sting1 deletion, not established for the VS-X4 NGLY1 drug arm.
Pharmacological survival findings in the paper involve a separate Trex1 model.
Post-weaning treatment preceded later progressive phenotype; no demonstrated reversal of established neuron loss.
Inducible postnatal model differs from congenital disease and other models.
NGLY1 pathology is not established to be fully corrected by STING inhibition.
JEM and PMC are one study.
records.value_capture_assessment: Exact asset identified; ownership, patents, freedom to operate, license availability, terms, and development package not established.
records.comparator: Cash for development capital; genetic NGLY1 correction and other translational approaches only as general scientific comparators, not evaluated investable assets.
records.next_decision_changing_question: Does an obtainable compound package exist with evidence supporting relevant human exposure and a credible clinical disease-modification proposition?
records.next_information_step: Bounded public evidence/ownership review; no outreach authorized or performed.
records.financing_and_time: Public evidence-and-rights conclusion may be inexpensive; clinical milestone budget and timing remain unknown.
advance_conditions: Evidence bridging model and human disease.
disconfirming_evidence: Benefit restricted to inducible model or preventive timing.
Important disease mechanisms persist despite STING blockade.
Human exposure or tolerability blocks chronic treatment.
Rights or terms prevent attainable value capture.
